units.zh: 王洛兒 車路頭 盧魯元 陳建 萬安國
units.en: Wang Luoer, Che Lutou, Lu Luyuan, Chen Jian, and Wan Anguo
units.literal: Wang Luoer, Che Lutou, Lu Luyuan, Chen Jian, Wan Anguo

units.zh: 王洛兒，京兆人也。
units.en: Wang Luoer came from Jingzhao.
units.literal: Wang Luoer was a man of Jingzhao.

units.zh: 少善騎射。
units.en: As a youth he was skilled in horsemanship and archery.
units.literal: In youth he excelled at mounted archery.

units.zh: 太宗在東宮，給事帳下，侍從遊獵，夙夜無怠。
units.en: While Emperor Taizong was still heir in the Eastern Palace, Luoer served in his personal staff, accompanying him on the hunt by day and night without slackening.
units.literal: When Taizong was in the Eastern Palace, he served in the tent staff, attending hunts, never idle from dawn to night.

units.zh: 性謹愿，未嘗有過。
units.en: He was by nature careful and dutiful and never once gave offense.
units.literal: His nature was cautious and sincere; he never had faults.

units.zh: 太宗嘗獵于灅南，乘冰而濟，冰陷沒馬，洛兒投水，奉太宗出岸。
units.en: Once when Emperor Taizong was hunting at Shuainan and crossed a river on the ice, the ice broke and his horse went under; Luoer plunged into the water and brought the emperor safely to shore.
units.literal: Taizong once hunted at Shuainan, crossing on ice; the ice gave way and submerged the horse; Luoer threw himself into the water and bore Taizong out to the bank.

units.zh: 水沒洛兒，殆將凍死，太宗解衣以賜之。
units.en: The water closed over Luoer and he was nearly frozen to death; the emperor stripped off his own garment and gave it to him.
units.literal: The water submerged Luoer and he nearly froze to death; Taizong removed his coat to grant him.

units.zh: 自是恩寵日隆。
units.en: From that time his favor and patronage grew ever greater.
units.literal: From then on favor daily increased.

units.zh: 天賜末，太宗出居于外，洛兒晨夜侍衞，無須臾違離，恭勤發於至誠。
units.en: Near the end of the Tiansi reign, when Emperor Taizong was forced to live outside the palace, Luoer guarded him morning and night without leaving his side for an instant, his reverent service springing from the deepest loyalty.
units.literal: At the end of Tiansi, Taizong went out to dwell elsewhere; Luoer attended day and night without a moment's departure, diligence born of utmost sincerity.

units.zh: 元紹之逆，太宗左右唯洛兒與車路頭而已。
units.en: During Yuan Shao's revolt, of all those close to Emperor Taizong only Luoer and Che Lutou remained.
units.literal: During Yuan Shao's rebellion, of Taizong's close attendants there were only Luoer and Che Lutou.

units.zh: 晝居山嶺，夜還洛兒家。
units.en: By day they hid in the mountains; by night they came back to Luoer's house.
units.literal: By day they dwelt in the hills; by night they returned to Luoer's home.

units.zh: 洛兒隣人李道潛相奉給，晨昏往復，眾庶頗知，喜而相告。
units.en: Luoer's neighbor Li Daoqian secretly provided for them, traveling to and fro morning and evening; word spread among the people, who rejoiced and told one another the news.
units.literal: Luoer's neighbor Li Daoqian supplied them in mutual support; going back and forth morning and evening, the multitude came to know and rejoiced, telling one another.

units.zh: 紹聞，收道斬之。
units.en: When Shao learned of this, he seized Daoqian and put him to death.
units.literal: Shao heard of it, seized Dao and executed him.

units.zh: 洛兒猶冒難往返京都，通問於大臣，大臣遂出奉迎，百姓奔赴。
units.en: Luoer still risked his life going back and forth to the capital to communicate with the chief ministers; they then came out to receive the emperor, and the common people rushed to join them.
units.literal: Luoer still braved difficulty traveling to and from the capital, communicating with ministers; the ministers then came out to welcome, and the people rushed to follow.

units.zh: 太宗還宮，社稷獲乂，洛兒有功焉。
units.en: When Emperor Taizong returned to the palace and the realm was restored to order, Luoer had earned a share of the credit.
units.literal: Taizong returned to the palace; the altars of state were settled; Luoer had merit therein.

units.zh: 太宗即位，拜散騎常侍。
units.en: After Emperor Taizong acceded to the throne, Luoer was appointed Regular Attendant.
units.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he was appointed Regular Attendant.

units.zh: 詔曰：「士處家必以孝敬為本，在朝則以忠節為先，不然，何以立身於當世，揚名於後代也。
units.en: An edict declared: "A man at home must root himself in filial piety and respect, and at court must put loyalty and integrity first; without these, how could he establish himself in his own age or leave a name to posterity?
units.literal: An edict said: "A gentleman at home must take filial piety and respect as root; in court he must take loyalty and integrity as foremost—otherwise how can he stand in his generation and spread his name to posterity?

units.zh: 散騎常侍王洛兒、車路頭等，服勤左右，十有餘年，忠謹恭肅，久而彌至，未嘗須臾之頃，有廢替之心。
units.en: Regular Attendant Wang Luoer, Che Lutou, and the rest have served diligently at my side for more than ten years, loyal, careful, and reverent, their devotion deepening with the years, and never for a moment have they shown any wish to leave my service.
units.literal: Regular Attendant Wang Luoer, Che Lutou and others served diligently at his side for more than ten years, loyal, respectful and solemn, growing more so over time; never for an instant did they have a heart of abandoning their post.

units.zh: 及在艱難，人皆易志，而洛兒等授命不移，貞操踰懇。
units.en: When times grew hard, others readily changed their allegiance, yet Luoer and his companions held to their charge without wavering, their steadfast loyalty surpassing mere duty.
units.literal: When in hardship, all men easily change purpose, but Luoer and the others received their mandate without shifting, their chaste conduct exceeding earnestness.

units.zh: 雖漢之樊灌，魏之許典無以加焉。
units.en: Not even Fan Kuai and Guan Ying of Han, nor Xu Chu and Dian Wei of Wei, could outdo them.
units.literal: Even Han's Fan Kuai and Guan Ying, Wei's Xu Dian—none could surpass them.

units.zh: 勤而不賞，何以奬勸將來為臣之節？
units.en: If such service goes unrewarded, how shall we encourage future generations of ministers in their duty?
units.literal: Diligence without reward—how can one encourage future generations in the integrity of ministers?

units.zh: 其賜洛兒爵新息公，加直意將軍。」
units.en: Let Luoer be enfeoffed as Duke of Xinxin and appointed General of Straight Intent."
units.literal: Therefore grant Luoer the title Duke of Xinxin, add General of Straight Intent."

units.zh: 又追贈其父為列侯，賜僮隸五十戶。
units.en: His father was also posthumously enfeoffed as a ranked marquis, with a grant of fifty households of retainers.
units.literal: Also posthumously enfeoff his father as a ranked marquis, grant fifty households of bondsmen.

units.zh: 永興五年卒。
units.en: He died in the fifth year of the Yongxing era.
units.literal: He died in the fifth year of Yongxing.

units.zh: 贈太尉、建平王，賜溫明祕器，載以轀輬車，使殿中衞士為之導從。
units.en: He was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant and Prince of Jianping, granted the lacquered coffin fittings of state, borne in the imperial hearse, with guards of the palace hall as his escort.
units.literal: Posthumously conferred Grand Commandant, Prince of Pingping; granted warm bright secret vessels, carried in the barred funeral carriage, with palace guards as escort.

units.zh: 太宗親臨哀慟者數四焉。
units.en: Emperor Taizong came in person to mourn him, weeping again and again.
units.literal: Taizong in person came to mourn, weeping several times.

units.zh: 乃鴆其妻周氏，與洛兒合葬。
units.en: He then had Luoer's wife, Lady Zhou, compelled to take poison and buried her with him in a joint grave.
units.literal: He then had Luoer's wife Lady Zhou poisoned and buried with Luoer.

units.zh: 子長成，襲爵。
units.en: His son Changcheng inherited the title.
units.literal: His son Changcheng inherited the title.

units.zh: 卒，無子。
units.en: He died leaving no son.
units.literal: He died without sons.

units.zh: 弟德成，襲爵。
units.en: His younger brother Decheng inherited the title.
units.literal: His younger brother Decheng inherited the title.

units.zh: 徙為建城公，加鎮遠將軍。
units.en: He was reassigned as Duke of Jiancheng and appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant.
units.literal: He was transferred to Duke of Jiancheng, added General Who Pacifies the Distant.

units.zh: 官至散騎常侍，典作長安。
units.en: He rose to Regular Attendant and supervised construction works at Chang'an.
units.literal: He reached the office of Regular Attendant and oversaw construction at Chang'an.

units.zh: 真君十一年卒。
units.en: He died in the eleventh year of the Zhenjun era.
units.literal: He died in the eleventh year of Zhenjun.

units.zh: 子定州，襲爵，降為建陽侯、安遠將軍。
units.en: His son Dingzhou inherited the title but was reduced to Marquis of Jianyang and made General Who Pacifies the Far.
units.literal: His son Dingzhou inherited the title, demoted to Marquis of Jianyang, General Who Pacifies the Far.

units.zh: 後定州弟升為侍御中散，有寵於顯祖，以祖父洛兒著勳先朝，詔復定州爵為公。
units.en: Later Dingzhou's younger brother Sheng became an attendant in the imperial escort and won favor with Emperor Xianzu; because their grandfather Luoer had earned distinction under the previous reign, an edict restored Dingzhou's rank to duke.
units.literal: Later Dingzhou's younger brother Sheng became Attendant Scattered Cavalier in the Imperial Escort, favored by Emperor Xianzu; because grandfather Luoer had merit in the previous dynasty, an edict restored Dingzhou's title to duke.

units.zh: 高祖初，為長安鎮將。
units.en: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he served as garrison commander of Chang'an.
units.literal: Early in Emperor Gaozu's reign, he was General Who Guards Chang'an.

units.zh: 卒。
units.en: He died.
units.literal: He died.

units.zh: 子陵，襲升爵。
units.en: His son Ling inherited the title that Sheng had held.
units.literal: His son Ling inherited Sheng's title.

units.zh: [1]承明初，遷監御長，賜爵始新子，加寧朔將軍、員外散騎常侍。
units.en: [1] At the opening of the Chengming era he was made supervisor of the imperial guard, enfeoffed as Viscount of Shixin, and appointed General Who Pacifies the North and extraordinary Regular Attendant.
units.literal: [1] At the beginning of Chengming, he was transferred to Supervisor of the Imperial Guard, granted the title Viscount of Shixin, added General Who Pacifies the North and Extraordinary Regular Attendant.

units.zh: 卒。
units.en: He died.
units.literal: He died.

units.zh: 車路頭，代人也。
units.en: Che Lutou was a native of Dai.
units.literal: Che Lutou was a man of Dai.

units.zh: 少以忠厚選給東宮，為太宗帳下帥。
units.en: In his youth he was chosen for the Eastern Palace on account of his honesty and loyalty and became commander of Emperor Taizong's personal guard.
units.literal: In youth, for his honesty and kindness he was selected to serve the Eastern Palace as Tent Commander under Taizong.

units.zh: 善自修立，謹慎無過。
units.en: He cultivated himself diligently and was careful never to give offense.
units.literal: He was good at cultivating himself, cautious and without fault.

units.zh: 天賜末，太宗出於外，路頭隨侍竭力。
units.en: Near the end of the Tiansi reign, when Emperor Taizong was forced out of the palace, Lutou followed and served him with all his strength.
units.literal: At the end of Tiansi, Taizong lived outside; Lutou followed and served with all his strength.

units.zh: 及太宗即位，拜為散騎常侍，賜爵金鄉公，加忠意將軍。
units.en: When Emperor Taizong acceded, Lutou was appointed Regular Attendant, enfeoffed as Duke of Jinxiang, and made General of Loyal Intent.
units.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he was appointed Regular Attendant, granted the title Duke of Jinxiang, added General of Loyal Intent.

units.zh: 後改為宣城公。
units.en: He was later reassigned as Duke of Xuancheng.
units.literal: Later he was changed to Duke of Xuancheng.

units.zh: 太宗性明察，羣臣多以職事遇譴，至有杖罰，故路頭優遊不任事，侍宿左右，從容談笑而已。
units.en: Emperor Taizong was keen and exacting; many officials were punished for faults in their duties, some even beaten with the staff, so Lutou held no active post and merely kept night watch at the emperor's side, passing the time in easy talk and laughter.
units.literal: Taizong's nature was sharp in perception; many officials were punished for their duties, even to beating; therefore Lutou leisurely did not take office, staying by his side at night, merely conversing and laughing at ease.

units.zh: 路頭性無害，每至評獄處理，常獻寬恕之議，以此見重於朝。
units.en: Lutou was by nature gentle and harmless; whenever cases came before him for judgment he would urge leniency, and for this he was held in high regard at court.
units.literal: Lutou's nature was harmless; whenever he reached verdicts and judgments he often offered lenient views, and thus was honored at court.

units.zh: 太宗亦敬納之，寵待隆厚，賞賜無數，當時功臣親幸莫及。
units.en: Emperor Taizong likewise respected and heeded him; his favor was lavish and his gifts beyond counting, and among the meritorious ministers of the day none enjoyed such intimacy.
units.literal: Taizong also respected and accepted this; favor was thick, rewards countless; among meritorious officials of the time none matched his intimacy.

units.zh: 泰常六年卒。
units.en: He died in the sixth year of the Taichang era.
units.literal: He died in the sixth year of Taichang.

units.zh: 太宗親臨哀慟。
units.en: Emperor Taizong came in person to mourn him.
units.literal: Taizong in person came to mourn.

units.zh: 贈侍中、左衞大將軍、太師、宣城王，諡曰忠貞。
units.en: He was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant, Grand General of the Left Guard, Grand Preceptor, and Prince of Xuancheng, with the posthumous title Loyal and True.
units.literal: Posthumously conferred Palace Attendant, Grand General of the Left Guard, Grand Preceptor, Prince of Xuancheng; posthumous name Loyal and True.

units.zh: 喪禮一依安城王叔孫俊故事。
units.en: The funeral rites followed entirely the precedent set for Prince Ancheng, Shusun Jun.
units.literal: Mourning rites wholly followed the precedent of Prince of Ancheng Shusun Jun.

units.zh: 陪葬金陵。
units.en: He was buried beside the emperor at Jinling.
units.literal: Buried alongside at Jinling.

units.zh: 子眷襲爵。
units.en: His son Juan inherited the title.
units.literal: His son Juan inherited the title.

units.zh: 盧魯元，昌黎徒河人也。
units.en: Lu Luyuan came from Tuhe in Changli commandery.
units.literal: Lu Luyuan was a man of Tuhe in Changli.

units.zh: 曾祖副鳩，仕慕容垂為尚書令、臨澤公。
units.en: His great-grandfather Fuchiu had served Murong Chui as Director of the Secretariat and been enfeoffed as Duke of Linze.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Fuchiu served Murong Chui as Director of the Secretariat and Duke of Linze.

units.zh: 祖父並至大官。
units.en: His grandfather and father both rose to high office.
units.literal: His grandfather and father both reached great office.

units.zh: 魯元敏而好學，寬和有雅度。
units.en: Luyuan was quick-witted and fond of study, magnanimous and possessed of cultivated bearing.
units.literal: Luyuan was clever and loved learning, generous and had refined bearing.

units.zh: 太宗時，選為直郎。
units.en: During Emperor Taizong's reign he was chosen as a direct attendant.
units.literal: In Taizong's time he was selected as Direct Gentleman.

units.zh: 以忠謹給侍東宮，恭勤盡節，世祖親愛之。
units.en: For his loyalty and discretion he was assigned to the Eastern Palace, where he served with reverent diligence; Emperor Shizu held him in special affection.
units.literal: For loyalty and prudence he was assigned to serve the Eastern Palace with respectful diligence in utmost integrity; Emperor Shizu cherished him.

units.zh: 及即位，以為中書侍郎，拾遺左右，寵待彌深，而魯元益加謹肅，世祖逾親信之，內外大臣莫不敬憚焉。
units.en: When Shizu took the throne, Luyuan was made Vice Director of the Secretariat with the duty of remonstrance at the emperor's side; his favor deepened, yet Luyuan grew only more grave and careful, and the emperor trusted him all the more, so that ministers within and without the court all regarded him with respect and awe.
units.literal: Upon taking the throne, he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, remonstrance at left and right; favor grew deeper, while Luyuan grew more solemn; Emperor Shizu trusted him ever more; inward and outward ministers none did not respect and fear him.

units.zh: 性多容納，善與人交，好掩人之過，揚人之美，由是公卿咸親附之。
units.en: He was by nature forbearing and open-handed, skilled at friendship, apt to cover others' faults and praise their virtues, and for this the highest officials all sought his company.
units.literal: His nature was much tolerant; he was good at making friends, liked covering others' faults and praising others' virtues; thereby all chief ministers drew close to him.

units.zh: 魯元以工書，有文才，累遷中書監，領祕書事。
units.en: For his skill in calligraphy and literary talent Luyuan was repeatedly promoted, eventually becoming Director of the Secretariat and overseer of the imperial library.
units.literal: Luyuan for skill in calligraphy and literary talent was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Secretariat, overseeing Secretariat affairs.

units.zh: 賜爵襄城公，加散騎常侍、右將軍。
units.en: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangcheng and appointed Regular Attendant and General of the Right.
units.literal: Granted the title Duke of Xiangcheng, added Regular Attendant and General of the Right.

units.zh: 賜其父為信都侯。
units.en: His father was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xindu.
units.literal: His father was granted the title Marquis of Xindu.

units.zh: 從征赫連昌。
units.en: He accompanied the campaign against Helian Chang.
units.literal: He followed the campaign against Helian Chang.

units.zh: 世祖親追擊之，入其城門，魯元隨世祖出入。
units.en: Emperor Shizu personally pursued the enemy and entered their city gate, with Luyuan attending him in and out.
units.literal: Emperor Shizu personally pursued him, entering the city gate; Luyuan followed Emperor Shizu in and out.

units.zh: 是日，微魯元，幾至危殆。
units.en: That day, but for Luyuan, the emperor would have come to grievous harm.
units.literal: That day, without Luyuan he would nearly have reached peril.

units.zh: 從征平涼，以功拜征北大將軍，加侍中。
units.en: On the campaign against Pingliang he was rewarded with the post of General Who Campaigns North and Palace Attendant.
units.literal: He followed the campaign to Pingliang; for merit he was appointed General Who Campaigns North, added Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 後遷太保、錄尚書事。
units.en: He was later made Grand Guardian and put in charge of recording Secretariat affairs.
units.literal: Later he was transferred to Grand Guardian and recorded Secretariat affairs.

units.zh: 世祖貴異之，常從征伐，出入臥內。
units.en: Emperor Shizu prized him above others, taking him on campaign after campaign and admitting him to his private chambers.
units.literal: Emperor Shizu held him in exceptional esteem, often followed on campaigns, entering and leaving his sleeping quarters.

units.zh: 每有平殄，輒以功賞賜僮隸，前後數百人，布帛以萬計。
units.en: Whenever a campaign ended in victory he would reward Luyuan with household retainers for his service—several hundred in all over the years—and silk cloth by the tens of thousands.
units.literal: Whenever there was pacification he would reward with bondsmen for merit, several hundred before and after, silk cloth by tens of thousands.

units.zh: 世祖臨幸其第，不出旬日。
units.en: Emperor Shizu visited his mansion and stayed for nearly ten days.
units.literal: Emperor Shizu visited his residence and did not leave for ten days.

units.zh: 欲其居近，易於往來，乃賜甲第於宮門南。
units.en: Wishing him to live close at hand for easy visits, the emperor granted him a grand residence just south of the palace gate.
units.literal: Wishing him to dwell nearby for easy coming and going, he granted a fine mansion south of the palace gate.

units.zh: 衣食車馬，皆乘輿之副。
units.en: His food, clothing, carriages, and horses were all of the same quality as the emperor's own.
units.literal: Food, clothing, carriages and horses were all surplus of the imperial equipage.

units.zh: 真君三年冬，車駕幸陰山，魯元以疾不從。
units.en: In winter of the third year of Zhenjun, the emperor visited Yinshan, but Luyuan stayed behind because he was ill.
units.literal: In winter of the third year of Zhenjun, the imperial carriage visited Yinshan, and Luyuan did not accompany it because of illness.

units.zh: 侍臣問疾送醫藥，傳驛相屬於路。
units.en: Attendants were sent to ask after him and deliver medicine, with relay messengers following one another along the route.
units.literal: Attending ministers inquired after his illness and sent medicines, with relay messengers following one another along the road.

units.zh: 及薨，世祖甚悼惜之。
units.en: When Luyuan died, Emperor Shizu mourned him deeply.
units.literal: When he died, Emperor Shizu greatly mourned and regretted him.

units.zh: 還，臨其喪，哭之哀慟。
units.en: On his return, the emperor went to the mourning rites and wept for him with great sorrow.
units.literal: On returning, he attended the mourning and wept for him in bitter grief.

units.zh: 東西二宮命太官日送奠，晨昏哭臨，訖則備奏鐘鼓伎樂。
units.en: The Eastern and Western Palaces ordered the Imperial Provisioner to send offerings each day; morning and evening they came to mourn and weep, and afterward bells, drums, and music were performed in full.
units.literal: The Eastern and Western Palaces ordered the Imperial Provisioner to send offerings daily, attended and wept morning and evening, and when this was finished fully performed bells, drums, and music.

units.zh: 輿駕比葬三臨之。
units.en: Before the burial, the emperor came in person to mourn him three times.
units.literal: Before the burial, the imperial carriage came to mourn him three times.

units.zh: 喪禮依安城王故事，而贈送有加。
units.en: His funeral rites followed the precedent for Prince Ancheng, with still greater posthumous gifts and honors.
units.literal: The funeral rites followed the precedent for Prince Ancheng, but the posthumous gifts and send-off were increased.

units.zh: 贈襄城王，諡曰孝。
units.en: He was posthumously made Prince of Xiangcheng, with the posthumous name Xiao.
units.literal: Posthumously granted Prince of Xiangcheng; posthumous name Xiao.

units.zh: 葬於崞山，為建碑闕。
units.en: He was buried at Guo Mountain, where a stele and ceremonial gate towers were erected for him.
units.literal: Buried at Guo Mountain, and a stele and gateway towers were built for him.

units.zh: 自魏興，貴臣恩寵，無與為比。
units.en: Since the founding of Wei, no honored minister had received favor comparable to his.
units.literal: Since the rise of Wei, among honored ministers, none had favor and privilege comparable to his.

units.zh: 子統襲爵。
units.en: His son Tong succeeded to the title.
units.literal: His son Tong inherited the title.

units.zh: 少子內，給侍東宮，恭宗深昵之，常與臥起同衣。
units.en: His younger son Nei served in the Eastern Palace; Crown Prince Gongzong was deeply attached to him and often shared his bed, rising together and even wearing the same garments.
units.literal: His younger son Nei served the Eastern Palace; Prince Gongzong was deeply fond of him, often sharing bed, rising and clothes.

units.zh: 父子有寵兩宮，勢傾天下。
units.en: Father and son enjoyed favor in both palaces, and their influence overshadowed the court.
units.literal: Father and son had favor in both palaces; their power tilted the realm.

units.zh: 內性寬厚，有父風，而恭順不及。
units.en: Nei was generous by nature and resembled his father in manner, yet he lacked his father's reverent obedience.
units.literal: Nei's nature was generous, had his father's manner, but did not match his father's deference.

units.zh: 正平初，宮臣伏誅，世祖以魯元故，唯殺內而厚撫其兄弟。
units.en: Early in the Zhengping era, when palace officials were put to death, Emperor Shizu, for Luyuan's sake, executed only Nei and treated his brothers with generous favor.
units.literal: At the beginning of Zhengping, palace officials were executed; Emperor Shizu for Luyuan's sake only killed Nei and treated his brothers generously.

units.zh: 統以父任，侍東宮。
units.en: Tong entered service in the Eastern Palace through his father's position.
units.literal: Tong, through his father's position, served in the Eastern Palace.

units.zh: 世祖以元舅陽平王杜超女，南安長公主所生妻之。
units.en: Emperor Shizu married him to a daughter of Du Chao, Prince of Yangping and imperial maternal uncle, who had been born to Grand Princess Nan'an.
units.literal: Emperor Shizu took the daughter of Du Chao, Prince of Yangping and the imperial maternal uncle, born to Grand Princess Nan'an, and married her to him.

units.zh: 車駕親自臨送，太官設供具，賜賚以千計。
units.en: The emperor personally attended the send-off; the Imperial Provisioner laid out the wedding provisions, and gifts were bestowed by the thousand.
units.literal: The imperial carriage personally came to send them off; the Imperial Provisioner set out the supplies, and gifts were counted by the thousand.

units.zh: 高宗即位，典選部、主客二曹。
units.en: After Emperor Gaozong came to the throne, Tong oversaw the Selection and Host and Guest bureaus.
units.literal: When Emperor Gaozong came to the throne, he managed the two bureaus of Selection and Host and Guest.

units.zh: 興安二年卒。
units.en: He died in the second year of the Xing'an era.
units.literal: He died in the second year of Xing'an.

units.zh: 贈襄城王，諡曰景。
units.en: He was posthumously made Prince of Xiangcheng, with the posthumous name Jing.
units.literal: He was posthumously presented as Prince of Xiangcheng, with the posthumous name Jing.

units.zh: 無子。
units.en: He had no sons.
units.literal: He had no son.

units.zh: 弟彌娥，襲爵。
units.en: His younger brother Mie inherited the title.
units.literal: His younger brother Mie inherited the title.

units.zh: 拜北鎮都將。
units.en: He was appointed commander of the northern garrison.
units.literal: He was appointed General of the Northern Garrison.

units.zh: 卒，贈襄城王，諡曰恭。
units.en: He died and was posthumously honored as Prince of Xiangcheng, with the posthumous title Respectful.
units.literal: He died; posthumously granted Prince of Xiangcheng; posthumous name Respectful.

units.zh: 子興仁襲爵。
units.en: His son Xingren inherited the title.
units.literal: His son Xingren inherited the title.

units.zh: 陳建，代人也。
units.en: Chen Jian was a native of Dai.
units.literal: Chen Jian was a man of Dai.

units.zh: 祖渾，太祖末為右衞將軍。
units.en: His grandfather Hun, in the last years of Emperor Taizu, served as General of the Right Guard.
units.literal: His grandfather Hun, at the end of Taizu, was General of the Right Guard.

units.zh: 父陽，尚書。
units.en: His father Yang held the post of Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: His father Yang was Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 建以善騎射，擢為三郎。
units.en: For his skill in horsemanship and archery, Jian was promoted to the rank of third-grade guard.
units.literal: Jian for skill in mounted archery was promoted to Third-Rank Guard.

units.zh: 稍遷下大夫、內行長。
units.en: He was gradually promoted to lower grand master and chief of the inner service.
units.literal: He was gradually promoted to Lower Grand Master and Chief of Inner Service.

units.zh: 世祖討山胡白龍，意甚輕之，單將數十騎登山臨嶮，每日如此。
units.en: When Emperor Shizu campaigned against the Mountain Hu chieftain Bai Long, he took the enemy lightly and would ride up alone with only a few dozen horsemen to overlook the steep passes, doing so day after day.
units.literal: Emperor Shizu campaigned against the Mountain Hu Bai Long and thought it quite light; alone he led several dozen horsemen up the mountain overlooking the defile, daily so.

units.zh: 白龍乃伏壯士十餘處，出於不意，世祖墮馬，幾至不測。
units.en: Bai Long had hidden stalwart warriors in more than ten places; they sprang out unexpectedly, the emperor was thrown from his horse, and he came within a hair's breadth of disaster.
units.literal: Bai Long then hid stalwart warriors in more than ten places, emerging unexpectedly; Emperor Shizu fell from his horse and nearly reached beyond reckoning.

units.zh: 建以身捍賊，大呼奮擊，殺賊數人，身被十餘創。
units.en: Jian shielded the emperor with his own body, shouting as he fought fiercely, killed several of the enemy, and took more than ten wounds himself.
units.literal: Jian with his body defended against the bandits, shouted and struck fiercely, killed several bandits, his body received more than ten wounds.

units.zh: 世祖壯之，賜戶二十。
units.en: Emperor Shizu admired his courage and granted him twenty tax households.
units.literal: Emperor Shizu admired him and granted twenty households.

units.zh: 高宗初，賜爵阜城侯，加冠軍將軍。
units.en: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozong's reign he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fucheng and appointed Champion General.
units.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozong's reign, he was granted the title Marquis of Fucheng, added Champion General.

units.zh: 出為幽州刺史，假秦郡公。
units.en: He was sent out as governor of You Province with the acting title Duke of Qin commandery.
units.literal: He was sent out as Governor of You Province, acting Duke of Qin Commandery.

units.zh: 高宗以建貪暴懦弱，遣使就州罰杖五十。
units.en: Because Jian was greedy, cruel, and weak in character, Emperor Gaozong sent an envoy to his province to have him beaten with fifty strokes of the staff.
units.literal: Emperor Gaozong because Jian was greedy, brutal and weak, sent a messenger to the prefecture to punish with fifty cane strokes.

units.zh: 高祖初，徵為尚書右僕射，加侍中，進爵趙郡公。
units.en: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was recalled as Vice Director of the Right Secretariat, appointed Palace Attendant, and raised to Duke of Zhao commandery.
units.literal: Early in Emperor Gaozu's reign, he was summoned as Vice Director of the Secretariat Right, added Palace Attendant, advanced to Duke of Zhao Commandery.

units.zh: 建與侍中尚書、晉陽侯元仙德，殿中尚書、長樂王穆亮，比部尚書、平原王陸叡密表曰：[2]「皇天輔德，命集大魏。
units.en: Jian joined with Palace Attendant and Secretariat Director Yuan Xiande, Marquis of Jinyang, Director of Palace Affairs Prince Changhe Mu Liang, and Director of Justice Prince Pingyuan Lu Rui in a secret memorial that read: [2] "High Heaven assists the virtuous, and the mandate has settled upon Great Wei.
units.literal: Jian with Palace Attendant and Secretariat Director, Marquis of Jinyang Yuan Xiande, Director of Palace Affairs Changhe Prince Mu Liang, and Director of Justice Pingyuan Prince Lu Rui submitted a secret memorial saying: [2] "High Heaven assists virtue; the mandate gathers on Great Wei.

units.zh: 臣等祖父翼贊初興，勤過蜀漢，誓固山河，享茲景福，寵辱休戚，與國均焉。
units.en: Our grandfathers aided the dynasty at its founding, their service surpassing even the ministers of Shu-Han; they swore to hold the realm firm and have enjoyed this bright fortune, sharing honor and disgrace, weal and woe, equally with the state.
units.literal: We subjects' grandfathers aided the founding, their diligence exceeding Shu-Han, swore to secure mountains and rivers, enjoy this bright fortune; favor and disgrace, weal and woe, are equal with the state.

units.zh: 臣以凡近，識無遠達，階藉先寵，遂荷今任，彼己之譏，播於羣口。
units.en: I am a man of common station and shallow understanding, yet I have climbed on my family's former favor to bear my present office; reproaches comparing me with worthier men spread among the multitude.
units.literal: Your subject by ordinary proximity, knowledge without far sight, steps on former favor's stairs, thus bears present burden; comparison to others' reproach spreads among the multitude.

units.zh: 仰感生成，俯自策厲，顧省駑鈍，終於無益。
units.en: I look up, moved by the grace the throne has shown me, and bend my efforts to improve myself, yet when I examine my own dull inadequacy I find it avails nothing in the end.
units.literal: Looking up, moved by the emperor's nurturing; bowing down, I spur myself on; reflecting on my dull incompetence, in the end of no benefit.

units.zh: 然飲冰驚寐，實懷慚負。
units.en: Yet I lie awake in distress as though drinking ice, truly burdened with shame and remorse.
units.literal: Yet drinking ice and starting from sleep, truly harboring shame and debt.

units.zh: 至於願。
units.en: As for my wish—
units.literal: As to my wish.

units.zh: 天高地厚，何日忘之。
units.en: Heaven is high and earth is deep—on what day could I ever forget such kindness?
units.literal: Heaven high and earth thick—on what day could I forget it?

units.zh: 自永嘉之末，封豕橫噬，馬叡南據，奄有荊楚。
units.en: Since the end of the Yongjia era, barbarian invaders have ravaged the land unchecked, while Sima Rui seized the south and came to hold Jing and Chu.
units.literal: From the end of Yongjia, the great boar rampaged across the land; Sima Rui seized the south and swallowed Jing and Chu.

units.zh: 及桓劉跋扈，禍難相繼。
units.en: When the houses of Huan and Liu grew arrogant and overbearing, disasters followed one after another.
units.literal: When Huan and Liu grew overbearing, calamities followed one upon another.

units.zh: 岱宗隔望秩之敬，青徐限見德之風。
units.en: Mount Tai stood cut off from the rites of ranked sacrifice, and Qing and Xu were barred from the transforming breeze of imperial virtue.
units.literal: Mount Tai was cut off from ranked sacrifices; Qing and Xu were barred from the wind of transforming virtue.

units.zh: 獻文皇帝髫齓龍飛，道光率土，干戚暫舞，淮海從風，車書既同，華裔將一。
units.en: Emperor Xianwen took the throne while still a child; his radiance shone across the realm; when arms were briefly raised, the Huai and Hai regions bowed to the wind; chariots and writing were unified, and Chinese and barbarian were on the verge of becoming one.
units.literal: Emperor Xianwen in infancy rose like a dragon; his way illuminated the entire realm; arms briefly danced and Huai and Hai followed the wind; chariots and documents were unified, Chinese and barbarian would become one.

units.zh: 昊天不弔，奄背萬邦。
units.en: Bright Heaven showed no mercy, and he suddenly abandoned the myriad realms.
units.literal: Bright Heaven did not pity; suddenly he turned his back on the myriad states.

units.zh: 竊聞劉昱夭亡，權臣殺害，思正之民，翹想罔極。
units.en: I have heard that Liu Yu died young, murdered by powerful ministers, and that upright people throughout the land yearn for him beyond measure.
units.literal: I have privately heard Liu Yu died young, slaughtered by powerful ministers; people who think rightly long for him beyond measure.

units.zh: 愚謂時不再來，機宜易失，毫分之差，致悔千里。
units.en: I humbly believe that time will not return, that opportunity is easily lost, and that an error no wider than a hair can bring regret a thousand leagues hence.
units.literal: I foolishly think the time will not come again, opportunity easily lost—a hairsbreadth slip leads to regret a thousand li away.

units.zh: 天與不取，反受其咎，所謂見而不作，過在介石者也。
units.en: He who fails to seize what Heaven offers will suffer punishment in return; as the saying goes, to see yet not act is a fault as plain as a jie stone set in the sun.
units.literal: Heaven's gift not taken—one receives punishment in return; what is called seeing yet not acting, the fault lies in the alert jie stone.

units.zh: 宜簡雄將，號令八方。
units.en: We should select bold commanders and issue orders to the eight directions.
units.literal: One should select fierce generals and command the eight directions.

units.zh: 義陽王臣昶，深悟存亡，遠同孫氏。
units.en: Prince Yiyang, our subject Yuan Chang, deeply understands the stakes of survival and ruin and is well suited to follow the example of Sun Quan.
units.literal: Prince of Yiyang, our subject Chang, deeply comprehends survival and destruction, far sharing the Sun clan's example.

units.zh: 苟歷運響從，則吳會可定，脫事有難成，則振旅而返。
units.en: If the dynasty's fortune answers and the people respond, Wu and Kuaiji can be secured; if the enterprise proves difficult, the army can be rallied and withdrawn.
units.literal: If the dynasty's fortune responds and follows, then Wu and Hui can be settled; if matters are hard to accomplish, then rally the army and return.

units.zh: 進可以揚義聲於四海，退可以通德信於遐裔。
units.en: Advancing, we can spread righteous renown to the four seas; retreating, we can extend virtue and good faith to distant lands.
units.literal: Advancing can spread righteous fame through the four seas; retreating can extend virtue and trust to distant realms.

units.zh: 宜乘之會，運鍾今日，如合聖聽，乞速施行。
units.en: This is the moment to act, for fortune has struck today; if this accords with Your Majesty's judgment, I beg that it be carried out at once.
units.literal: One should seize this opportune moment—fortune rings today; if it fits the sage's hearing, I beg swift implementation.

units.zh: 脫忤天心，願存臣表，徐觀後驗，賞罰隨焉。」
units.en: If it runs counter to Heaven's intent, I ask only that this memorial be kept on record so that later results may be weighed, and reward or punishment may follow accordingly."
units.literal: If it goes against Heaven's heart, I wish to preserve this subject's memorial and slowly observe later verification; reward and punishment will follow."

units.zh: 高祖嘉之。
units.en: Emperor Xiaowen commended the proposal.
units.literal: Emperor Gaozu praised it.

units.zh: 遷司徒、征西大將軍，進爵魏郡王。
units.en: Jian was promoted to Grand Minister of Education and General Who Campaigns West, and raised to Prince of Wei commandery.
units.literal: He was transferred to Grand Minister of Education and General Who Campaigns West, advanced to Duke of Wei Commandery.

units.zh: 高祖與文明太后頻幸建第，賜建妻宴於後庭。
units.en: Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming often visited Jian's mansion, and the empress dowager granted banquets for Jian's wife in the rear palace.
units.literal: Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming frequently visited Jian's residence and granted his wife banquets in the rear court.

units.zh: 太和九年薨。
units.en: He died in the ninth year of the Taihe era.
units.literal: He died in the ninth year of Taihe.

units.zh: 子念，襲爵。
units.en: His son Nian inherited the title.
units.literal: His son Nian inherited the title.

units.zh: 為中山守，坐掠良人為御史中尉王顯所彈。
units.en: He served as administrator of Zhongshan and was impeached by Imperial Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian for seizing innocent people.
units.literal: He was Administrator of Zhongshan; for seizing good people he was impeached by Imperial Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian.

units.zh: 遇赦，免。
units.en: He was pardoned when an amnesty was declared.
units.literal: He encountered an amnesty and was pardoned.

units.zh: 爵除。
units.en: His noble title was revoked.
units.literal: His title was removed.

units.zh: 萬安國，代人也。
units.en: Wan Anguo was a native of Dai.
units.literal: Wan Anguo was a man of Dai.

units.zh: 祖真，世為酋帥，恒率部民從世祖征伐，以功除平西將軍、敦煌公，轉驃騎大將軍、儀同三司。
units.en: His grandfather Zhen had for generations been a tribal chieftain and regularly led his people to follow Emperor Shizu on campaign; for his service he was made General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Dunhuang, and later promoted to Grand General of Agile Cavalry with the privilege of the Three Departments.
units.literal: His grandfather Zhen for generations was tribal chief, constantly leading his tribesmen to follow Emperor Shizu on campaigns; for merit he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Dunhuang, transferred to Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Equal in Three Departments.

units.zh: 父振，尚高陽長公主，拜駙馬都尉。
units.en: His father Zhen married the Elder Princess of Gaoyang and was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.
units.literal: His father Zhen married the Elder Princess of Gaoyang and was appointed Commandant of Escort Cavalry.

units.zh: 遷散騎常侍、寧西將軍、長安鎮將，賜爵馮翊公。
units.en: He was promoted to Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the West, and garrison commander of Chang'an, and enfeoffed as Duke of Fengyi.
units.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the West, and Garrison Commander of Chang'an, granted the title Duke of Fengyi.

units.zh: 安國少明敏，有姿貌。
units.en: Anguo was clever and quick-witted in his youth and possessed a handsome appearance.
units.literal: Anguo in youth was clever and keen, and had good looks.

units.zh: 以國甥，復尚河南公主，拜駙馬都尉。
units.en: As a nephew of the imperial house by marriage, he also married the Princess of Henan and was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.
units.literal: As the emperor's nephew by marriage, he again married the Princess of Henan and was appointed Commandant of Escort Cavalry.

units.zh: 遷散騎常侍。
units.en: He was promoted to Regular Attendant.
units.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant.

units.zh: 顯祖特親寵之，與同臥起，為立第宅，賞賜至巨萬。
units.en: Emperor Xianzu favored him with special intimacy, sharing his bed and his daily routine, built him a mansion, and lavished rewards upon him to the sum of tens of thousands.
units.literal: Emperor Xianzu especially cherished him, sharing bed and rising with him, built a residence for him, and rewards reached tens of thousands.

units.zh: 超拜大司馬、大將軍，封安城王。
units.en: He was abruptly promoted to Grand Marshal and Grand General and enfeoffed as Prince of Ancheng.
units.literal: He was extraordinarily appointed Grand Marshal and Grand General, enfeoffed as Prince of Ancheng.

units.zh: 安國先與神部長奚買奴不平，承明初，矯詔殺買奴於苑中。
units.en: Anguo had long been at odds with Shenbu chieftain Xi Mainu; early in the Chengming era he forged an edict and had Mainu killed in the imperial park.
units.literal: Anguo had earlier been on bad terms with Shenbu Chief Xi Mainu; at the beginning of Chengming, he forged an edict and killed Mainu in the park.

units.zh: 高祖聞之，大怒，遂賜安國死。
units.en: When Emperor Xiaowen learned of this he was furious and ordered Anguo to take his own life.
units.literal: Emperor Gaozu heard of it, was greatly angered, and thereupon granted Anguo death.

units.zh: 年二十三。
units.en: He was twenty-three years old.
units.literal: He was twenty-three years old.

units.zh: 子翼，襲王爵。
units.en: His son Yi inherited the princely title.
units.literal: His son Yi inherited the princely title.

units.zh: 太和十五年薨。
units.en: He died in the fifteenth year of the Taihe era.
units.literal: He died in the fifteenth year of Taihe.

units.zh: 高祖以其父受寵先朝，特贈并州刺史。
units.en: Because his father had enjoyed favor under the previous reign, Emperor Xiaowen specially posthumously honored him as governor of Bing province.
units.literal: Emperor Gaozu because his father had received favor in the previous dynasty specially posthumously granted him Governor of Bing Province.

units.zh: 子纂，字輔興，襲，依例降為公。
units.en: His son Zuan, whose style name was Fuxing, inherited the title, which by regulation was reduced to duke.
units.literal: His son Zuan, style name Fuxing, inherited; according to precedent was reduced to duke.

units.zh: 世宗時，起家司徒倉曹參軍。
units.en: During Emperor Shizong's reign he entered service as registrar in the granary bureau of the Ministry of Education.
units.literal: In Emperor Shizong's time he began his career as Registrar of the Granary Bureau under the Minister of Education.

units.zh: 遷南秦平西府司馬、護軍長史，加右軍將軍。
units.en: He was promoted to military adviser of the Pacify-West headquarters in Southern Qin and chief clerk to the Protector Army, with the additional title General of the Right Army.
units.literal: He was transferred to Military Adviser of the Pacify-West Headquarters of Southern Qin and Chief Clerk of the Protector Army, added General of the Right Army.

units.zh: 正光二年卒。
units.en: He died in the second year of the Zhengguang era.
units.literal: He died in the second year of Zhengguang.

units.zh: 贈假節、征虜將軍、荊州刺史。
units.en: He was posthumously honored with the provisional staff of authority, the title General Who Captures Barbarians, and the post of governor of Jing province.
units.literal: Posthumously granted provisional staff, General Who Captures Barbarians, and Governor of Jing Province.

units.zh: 子金剛，襲。
units.en: His son Jingang inherited the title.
units.literal: His son Jingang inherited.

units.zh: 武定末，開府祭酒。
units.en: At the end of the Wuding era he served as libationer of an opening office.
units.literal: At the end of Wuding he was Libationer of the Opening Office.

units.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。
units.en: When the Northern Qi dynasty was founded, his rank was reduced according to precedent.
units.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his title was reduced according to precedent.

units.zh: 有嵇拔者，[4]世為紇奚部帥。
units.en: There was also Ji Ba, [4] who for generations had been chieftain of the Hexi tribe.
units.literal: There was Ji Ba, [4] for generations chief of the Hexi tribe.

units.zh: 其父根，皇始初率眾歸魏。
units.en: His father Gen, at the beginning of the Huangshi era, led his people to submit to Wei.
units.literal: His father Gen, at the beginning of Huangshi, led the multitude to submit to Wei.

units.zh: 太祖嘉之。
units.en: Emperor Taizu commended him for it.
units.literal: Taizu praised this.

units.zh: 尚昭成女，生子拔，卒於尚書令。
units.en: He married a daughter of Emperor Zhaocheng and fathered Ba, who died while serving as Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: He married a daughter of Zhaocheng and begot Ba, who died in the office of Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 拔尚華陰公主，生子敬。
units.en: Ba married the Princess of Huayin and fathered Jing.
units.literal: Ba married the Princess of Huayin and begot Jing.

units.zh: 元紹之逆也，主有功，超授敬大司馬、大將軍，封長樂王。
units.en: During Yuan Shao's revolt the princess rendered distinguished service, and Jing was abruptly promoted to Grand Marshal and Grand General and enfeoffed as Prince of Changle.
units.literal: During Yuan Shao's rebellion, the princess had merit; Jing was extraordinarily appointed Grand Marshal and Grand General, enfeoffed as Prince of Changle.

units.zh: 薨。
units.en: He died.
units.literal: He died.

units.zh: 子護，襲爵。
units.en: His son Hu inherited the title.
units.literal: His son Hu inherited the title.

units.zh: 拜外都大官。
units.en: He was appointed Grand Officer of the Outer Capital.
units.literal: He was appointed Grand Officer of the Outer Capital.

units.zh: 太和中，詔以護年邁，既未致仕，令依舊養老之例。
units.en: During the Taihe era an edict noted that Hu was advanced in years yet had not retired, and ordered that he be treated according to the established precedent for supporting elderly officials.
units.literal: In Taihe, an edict because Hu was aged and had not yet retired ordered him to follow the old precedent for supporting the elderly.

units.zh: 卒，子彥嗣。
units.en: He died, and his son Yan succeeded him.
units.literal: He died; his son Yan succeeded.

units.zh: 根事迹遺落，故略附云。
units.en: Because Gen's deeds have been lost from the record, they are only briefly appended here.
units.literal: Gen's deeds were lost and scattered; therefore they are briefly appended here.

units.zh: 史臣曰：王洛兒、車路頭、盧魯元、陳建，咸以誠至發衷，竭節危難，苟非志烈過人，亦何能以若此！
units.en: The historian writes: Wang Luoer, Che Lutou, Lu Luyuan, and Chen Jian all acted from sincere devotion of heart and gave their utmost loyalty in times of peril; had they not possessed resolution surpassing ordinary men, how could they have done as they did!
units.literal: The historian says: Wang Luoer, Che Lutou, Lu Luyuan, and Chen Jian all with utmost sincerity moved their inner hearts and exhausted their integrity in hardship; if not men of surpassing fierce resolve, how could they have done thus!

units.zh: 宜其生受恩遇，歿盡哀榮。
units.en: It is only fitting that in life they received imperial favor and in death the full honors of mourning.
units.literal: It is fitting that in life they received favor and in death full mourning honor.

units.zh: 至如安國，貴寵異於數子哉。
units.en: As for Anguo, his exalted favor stood apart even from these others.
units.literal: As for Anguo, his noble favor differed from these several men!

units.zh: 校勘記
units.en: Collation Notes
units.literal: Textual Collation Notes

units.zh: 子陵襲升爵 按上不言升封何爵，疑傳有脫文。
units.en: "Son Ling inherited Sheng's title": the text above does not say what title Sheng held; the biography appears to have lost wording here.
units.literal: "Son Ling inherited Sheng's title" — examining above, it does not state what title Sheng received; the biography is suspected to have lost text.

units.zh: 比部尚書平原王陸叡密表曰 冊府卷四七二
units.en: "Director of Justice Prince Pingyuan Lu Rui submitted a secret memorial" — Imperial Readings, juan 472
units.literal: "Director of Justice Pingyuan Prince Lu Rui submitted a secret memorial" — Imperial Readings, juan 472

units.zh: 〈五六二五頁〉
units.literal: 〈Page 5625〉

units.en: The character "bi" (justice bureau) appears as "bei" (north).
units.literal: "Bi" is written as "bei."

units.zh: 按陸叡為北部尚書，見卷四０本傳，疑作「北」是，但冊府宋本也作「比」，今不改。
units.en: Lu Rui served as Director of the Northern Secretariat, as seen in his main biography in juan 40; "bei" is probably correct, but the Song edition of Imperial Readings also reads "bi," so the text is left unchanged.
units.literal: Examining: Lu Rui was Director of the Northern Secretariat, seen in juan 40 main biography; it is suspected writing "bei" is correct, but the Song edition of Imperial Readings also writes "bi"; we do not change it now.

units.zh: 至於願 按句未完，與下文也不連貫，當有脫文，今於「願」下句斷。
units.en: "As to my wish": the sentence is incomplete and does not connect with what follows; text has clearly been lost, so a sentence break is made after "wish."
units.literal: "As to wish" — examining, the sentence is incomplete and does not connect with the text below; there should be lost text; we now break the sentence after "wish."

units.zh: 有嵇拔者 諸本「嵇」作「奚」，北史卷二五本傳作「嵇」。
units.en: "There was Ji Ba": various editions write "Ji" as "Xi," but the main biography in the History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 25, reads "Ji."
units.literal: "There was Ji Ba" — in various editions "ji" is written as "xi"; the main biography in History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 25, writes "ji."

units.zh: 按卷三太宗紀永興三年十二月甲午見「任城公嵇拔」，泰常四年甲戌，記「獻懷長公主子嵇敬封長樂王」，與此傳合。
units.en: Juan 3 of the Taizong Annals, twelfth month of Yongxing year 3 (day jiawu), records "Duke of Rencheng Ji Ba," and Taichang year 4 (day jiaxu) records "Ji Jing, son of the Elder Princess of Xianhuai, enfeoffed as Prince of Changle," which agrees with this biography.
units.literal: Examining: juan 3 Taizong Annals, twelfth month of Yongxing year 3, day jiawu, records "Duke of Rencheng Ji Ba"; Taichang year 4, day jiaxu, records "Son of the Elder Princess of Xianhuai Ji Jing enfeoffed as Prince of Changle" — matching this biography.

units.zh: 卷一一三官氏志：「紇奚氏後改為嵇氏。」
units.en: Juan 113, Offices and Clans: "The Hexi clan was later changed to the Ji clan."
units.literal: Juan 113 Offices and Clans Record: "The Hexi clan later was changed to the Ji clan."

units.zh: 這裏「奚」字乃涉下「紇奚部帥」而訛，今據北史改。
units.en: The character "Xi" here was corrupted under the influence of "Hexi tribal chief" below; it is corrected here on the authority of the History of the Northern Dynasties.
units.literal: Here the character "xi" was corrupted by influence from "Hexi tribal chief" below; now changed according to the History of the Northern Dynasties.

units.zh: 又傳失書嵇拔封爵。
units.en: The biography also fails to record Ji Ba's enfeoffment.
units.literal: Also the biography lost recording Ji Ba's enfeoffment.
